newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Q4 GDP rises 0.7 percent.
newsitem.headline: Canada Q4 GDP rises 0.7 percent.

text.p: Canada's real gross domestic product, at 1986 prices, rose a seasonally adjusted 0.7 percent in the fourth quarter from the third quarter of 1996, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
The economy grew by 2.9 percent at an annualized rate in the fourth quarter, the agency said.

A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 1.0 percent rise in the fourth quarter after the 0.8 percent rise in the previous quarter.
For the full year 1996 Canada's GDP rose 1.5 percent from 1995.
Statistics Canada said an upsurge in domestic demand led to the 0.7 percent quarterly rise in the GDP, despite a sudden drop in exports.
Domestic demand grew 1.8 percent in the quarter, its largest gain since the third quarter of 1987, but merchandise exports tumbled 3.4 percent in the last three months of 1996.
During the fourth quarter, demand was strong for consumer goods and services, residential construction, machinery and equipment and merchandise imports. Government spending continued to fall.
The quarterly rate of inflation for Canadian-made goods and services, as measured by the chain price index, was 0.3 percent. It was 1.6 percent for the whole of 1996, down from 2.0 percent in 1995.

Statistics Canada said economic activity picked up during the second half of 1996 as both domestic and foreign demand rose. Investment in machinery rose 11.0 percent in the year and investment in construction gained 11.5 percent.

Personal income grew by 2.1 percent in 1996, while taxes grew by 7.1 percent. As a result, disposable income gained only 1.0 percent. The personal savings rate fell to 4.6 percent in 1996, its lowest since 1961 and well below the 6.9 percent of 1995.
